memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The two men said to Lot, "Do you have anyone else here - sons-in-law, sons or daughters, or anyone else in the city who belongs to you? Get them out of here, because we are going to destroy this place. The outcry to the Lord against its people is so great that he has sent us to destroy it." - Gen 19:12-13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The angels reveal their mission plainly: judgement is coming, and they have come to rescue. Their first concern is for Lot's family - "Do you have anyone else here? Get them out." God's heart in judgement is to save all who belong to Him. Before the destruction falls, He seeks to gather out everyone who can be gathered.

Notice again the reason given: "The outcry to the Lord against its people is so great." Sodom's judgement was not arbitrary cruelty. Behind that outcry were countless victims of the city's violence and injustice, whose cries had reached heaven. God's judgement, however severe, was His response to real and terrible evil. He is a God of justice who will not let wickedness run forever.

But see the urgency of the rescue mission. The angels press Lot to gather everyone who belongs to him and flee. When God's grace comes to rescue, it comes with urgency, because judgement is real and time is short.

This is a picture of the gospel's urgency. There is a real judgement to come, and there is a real rescue offered in Christ. Like the angels urging Lot, we are sent to say to those we love, "Come out; be saved." Who in your life needs to hear the invitation to flee to safety in Christ? "Now is the time of God's favor, now is the day of salvation" (2 Cor 6:2).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you share God's urgency to see loved ones brought to safety in Christ?
- Who do you need to invite to "come out" and be saved?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, thank You that Your heart in judgement is to rescue all who belong to You. Give me Your urgency for those I love. Help me invite them to flee to the safety and salvation found in Christ.
Amen.
